ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, all vertices of the shape are on the grid points of a $3 \times 3$ square grid. Then, what is the sum of $\angle 1+\angle 2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, \\
from the given conditions, in right triangles $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle EFC$, \\
$\because \left\{\begin{array}{l}AB=EF\\ \angle B=\angle EFC=90^\circ\\ BC=FC\end{array}\right.$ \\
$\therefore$ right triangles $\triangle ABC\cong \triangle EFC$ (SAS) \\
$\therefore \angle 3=\angle 1$ \\
$\because \angle 2+\angle 3=45^\circ$ \\
$\therefore \angle 1+\angle 2=\angle 3+\angle 2=\boxed{45^\circ}$

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a 3×3 lattice. From the grid, ST? is not needed; the segment S C is a 1-by-1 diagonal, so it makes 45° with the horizontal. Introduce an auxiliary angle 3 at S between the horizontal grid line and the long slanted segment S R. The top small right triangle formed by T, C, R has legs 2 vertical units and 1 horizontal unit; the bottom right triangle formed by S, the horizontal projection, and R has legs 2 horizontal units and 1 vertical unit. These two right triangles are congruent up to rotation/reflection, so the acute angle at T, angle 1, equals auxiliary angle 3. Since angle 2 plus auxiliary angle 3 fills the 45° angle between S C and the horizontal, angle 1 + angle 2 = 45°.

所以 ∠1+∠2=∠3+∠2=45°。

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the figure: the figure is a 3×3 dashed grid. All vertices lie on grid points. The relevant vertex on the lower left can be denoted S, the lower end of the middle vertical line denoted C, the upper end of the vertical line denoted T, and the right-side vertex denoted R. In the figure, SC is a slanted line spanning 1 horizontal grid square and 1 vertical grid square; CT is a vertical segment; TR is a slanted line from T down to the right to R; SR is a long slanted line from S up to the right to R. Angle 1 is at point T, and angle 2 is near point S.

Then reason: because SC is 1 grid square horizontally and 1 grid square vertically in the grid, SC makes 45° with the horizontal line. Construct auxiliary angle 3 at point S, letting angle 3 be the angle between the horizontal line and the long slanted line SR. In this way, angle 2 and angle 3 together are exactly the angle between SC and the horizontal line, so ∠2+∠3=45°.

Observing the grid, the two right-angle sides of right triangle TCR are respectively 2 vertical grid squares and 1 horizontal grid square; while the two right-angle sides of the right triangle formed by S, R, and the horizontal projection of R are respectively 2 horizontal grid squares and 1 vertical grid square. The corresponding side lengths of the two are the same, only their positions are rotated or reflected, so the corresponding acute angles are equal, that is, ∠1=∠3.

Therefore ∠1+∠2=∠3+∠2=45°.
